memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been feeling unusually tired for the past month, with a pins-and-needles sensation in both feet and sometimes in my hands. I also notice I get short of breath climbing stairs. No fever or chest pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Patient presents with fatigue and peripheral tingling suspected vitamin B12 deficiency.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Reports of tiredness for 4 weeks, bilateral foot tingling, occasional hand paresthesia, mild exertional dyspnoea.

EXAMINATION: BP 122/78 mmHg, weight 70 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 24.8 (overweight). General appearance pale but alert. Cardiovascular and respiratory exams normal. Neurological: reduced vibration sense at distal toes, normal power.

IMPRESSION: Clinical picture consistent with vitamin B12 deficiency. Need to confirm with serum B12, MCV and haemoglobin.

ARRANGEMENTS: Order fasting serum vitamin B12, MCV and Hb. Advise balanced diet rich in animal proteins, start methylcobalamin after results. Return if worsening tingling, new chest pain, breathlessness >30 on exertion, or fever >38.5°C.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum vitamin B12: 150 pg/mL (reference 200-900). MCV: 102 fL (reference 80-100). Haemoglobin: 13.8 g/dL (reference 13.0-17.0).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg orally once daily. Duration: 3 months, then review.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Patient reports improved energy and reduced tingling after 3 months of supplementation.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Mild residual foot tingling only after prolonged standing, otherwise feeling well. No dyspnoea.

EXAMINATION: BP 118/76 mmHg, weight 70 kg, BMI 24.8 (overweight). Pale conjunctiva less noticeable. Neurological: vibration sense improved at toes, normal elsewhere.

IMPRESSION: Biochemical response likely good; need labs to confirm B12 repletion and haemogram stability.

ARRANGEMENTS: Order serum B12, MCV, Hb. Continue methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD. Advise maintain B12-rich diet, regular activity. Return if tingling worsens, new palpitations, fever >38.5°C, or unexplained bruising.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum vitamin B12: 420 pg/mL (reference 200-900). MCV: 94 fL (reference 80-100). Haemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL (reference 13.0-17.0).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg orally once daily. Continue for another 3 months, then reassess.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for review with Dr Priya Natarajan on 2025-11-05 at 10:30 AM. Patient to bring medication list.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Patient asymptomatic, feels energetic, no tingling.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: No current complaints.

EXAMINATION: BP 120/78 mmHg, weight 71 kg, BMI 25.2 (obese per Asian cut‑off). Advised on diet and activity. No pallor.

IMPRESSION: Vitamin B12 repletion maintained; weight slightly increased, BMI now obese – reinforce lifestyle.

ARRANGEMENTS: Continue methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD. Offer influenza vaccine (date to be noted in autumn). Return if new numbness, chest pain, breathlessness, or fever >38.5°C.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum vitamin B12: 180 pg/mL (reference 200-900). MCV: 100 fL (reference 80-100). Haemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL (reference 13.0-17.0).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Methylcobalamin increased to 2000 mcg orally once daily. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Patient admits missing doses intermittently, reports mild fatigue returning.

PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Occasional tiredness, no tingling.

EXAMINATION: BP 119/77 mmHg, weight 70 kg, BMI 24.8 (overweight).

IMPRESSION: Suboptimal B12 due to adherence; need to reinforce dosing and check levels.

ARRANGEMENTS: Order serum B12, MCV, Hb. Counsel on daily methylcobalamin 2000 mcg, set phone reminder. Return if fatigue worsens, new neurological symptoms, fever >38.5°C.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Serum vitamin B12: 350 pg/mL (reference 200-900). MCV: 96 fL (reference 80-100). Haemoglobin: 13.9 g/dL (reference 13.0-17.0).
